A constructive extension beyond the two-bin model

The strongest result is now a positive, recursively updated description of a class of interacting, replenished quantum systems, with an error bound for the complete permitted record under feedback.

The construction retains quantum noise correlations that the earlier isotropic source omitted. It then modifies those correlations only where they would prevent a positive classical evolution. The resulting error is controlled by the probability of reaching that region. A local version covers on-site interactions, cross-density interactions and record-dependent hopping on many-mode graphs.

This is a completed restricted theorem and a constructive numerical interface. Its present significance is mathematical: it connects a positive current-state representation to the actual quantum instrument, including subsequent records and controls. The conservative certified implementation is expensive, and economical conditioning on an arbitrary supplied record remains unresolved.

The earlier geometric identity, positive two-bin construction, separate quantum certificate and failed smaller representations remain intact. I copied actual working files byte for byte; I have not treated the inaccessible attachment controls as recovered.

High occupation alone is not the acquired classicality condition. Coordinate count, runtime, temperature and nonlinear strength remain separate resources.

3. The retained covariance changes an actual prediction

The new bridge is supported by a separate exact record calculation.

and first-port records in bins [0,1][0,1][0,1] and [1,3/2][1,3/2][1,3/2]. These monitored channels are a specified fraction 1/2721/2721/272 of the physical loss per mode.

The preserved exact coherence-band evaluator, used at this new parameter value with outward interval arithmetic, gives

for the positive-coupling protocol in both bins.

More specifically, for

A={both marks are nonzero and have the same sign},A=\{\text{both marks are nonzero and have the same sign}\},A={both marks are nonzero and have the same sign},

That difference exceeds the new source’s quantum allowance. Retaining the covariance therefore changes a permitted prediction; it does not merely improve a sufficient error coefficient.

This is an exact analytic certificate, not a newly acquired measurement or a Monte Carlo simulation of P^\widehat PP. The exact 2×22\times22×2 evaluator remains the preferable evaluator for this special experiment. The failed initial attempt to reuse a broader old interval assertion is preserved separately.

The constructive positive-law step is now complete for the stated regime. The remaining foundational obstacle is sharper: a bath can suppress departures from a positive coherent representation while leaving a complicated classical conditional law that still carries measurement-created information. The present theorem makes that law recursively generatable. It does not yet show when the law can be compressed into a small, economical state after an acquired history. Any such compression theorem must charge observation budget, controller access and preparation correlations—the donor-selection counterexample shows why those resources cannot be removed from the question.
